We need to review the design files for anomaly. Let's parse the netlist and spec carefully.

The spec describes Hades board: FCC = STM32H753VITx, NAVC = STM32F405RGTx. Power: MIC26903YJL-TR buck (5V), LD39200PU33R LDO (3V3). Current sense INA219AIDCNR across R1 = 10 mΩ. USB-UART bridges: otter_CH330 ×2. ESD/boot-select switch TDD01H0SB1R SPDT. HSE crystal ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3.

Now examine the netlist for anomalies.

First, the power section. Let's look at REG1 = MIC26903YJL-TR. Feedback divider: spec says "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)". R5 = 6k8, R6 = 1k3. Then Vout = 0.8*(1+6800/1300) = 0.8*(1+5.23) = 0.8*6.23 = 4.985 ≈ 5V. Good. R4 = 19k6 is in parallel with R5? Let's check nets. Net REG_FB: C7.2, R4.2, R5.2, R6.2, REG1.24 (FB). Net Net-(C6-Pad2): C6.2, R4.1. Hmm. So R4 connects from FB to ... Net-(C6-Pad2) which connects to C6.2. C6.1 is on REG_CS. Wait, let's look: C6 value 100n, footprint C_0805. Net REG_CS includes C5.1, C6.1, L1.1, REG1 pins SW_1..SW_6, CS. Net Net-(C6-Pad2) includes C6.2, R4.1. So R4 is between FB and the switch node? That's odd. Actually R4 = 19k6 in parallel with R5 (6k8)? Let's think: R5 is between +5V and FB (net REG_FB has R5.2, and +5V net has R5.1). R6 between GND and FB. So divider R5 (top, from Vout) and R6 (bottom). R4 = 19k6 in parallel with R5 would change Vout. But R4's other end is C6.2, and C6.1 is on REG_CS (switch node). Hmm, that's weird. Actually wait, maybe R4 is in parallel with R5? Let's check: R5 pin1 on +5V, pin2 on REG_FB. R4 pin1 on Net-(C6-Pad2), pin2 on REG_FB. C6 pin1 on REG_CS, pin2 on Net-(C6-Pad2). So R4 and C6 form an RC network from switch node to FB — that's a feedforward compensation capacitor? Actually typical MIC26903 design: FB divider with a feedforward cap C7 from Vout to FB (C7 = 4n7, net +5V and REG_FB — yes C7 pin1 on +5V, pin2 on REG_FB). That's the feedforward cap. Then R4 + C6: C6 from switch node to one end of R4, R4 from other end to FB. That's a different compensation network (RC from SW to FB). Hmm, that's plausible for some regulators. Actually wait, the spec note says "Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)". With R5=6k8, R6=1k3 → 4.98V. Good. R4 not mentioned. But R4+C6 network might be intentional. Hard to call anomaly.

Let's look at L1 = 15u, footprint SRP1265A-150M:INDPM135125X650N. Value matches spec "L = 15uH". Good.

Now check the buck regulator pin connections. REG1 pins: PVDD pin1 on Net-(REG1-PVDD) with C3.1. PGND pins 2,5,6,7,8,21,31 on GND. SW pins 4,9,10,11,12,29 on REG_CS. PVIN pins 13-19,30 on REG_VIN. VIN pin27 on REG_VIN. BST pin20 on REG_BST. CS pin22 on REG_CS. SGND pin23 on GND. FB pin24 on REG_FB. PG pin25 on REG_PG. EN pin26 on REG_EN. VDD pin28 on Net-(D1-A).

Hmm wait: SGND pin23 is on GND net. But spec says "Keep SGND and PGND separate - connect only at one location!" In the netlist, SGND (pin 23) is connected directly to GND, same net as PGND pins. That merges SGND and PGND. But is that an anomaly? The spec's layout note says keep separate in layout, connect at one point. In schematic, both might be on GND symbol but connected at single point in layout. KiCad netlist wouldn't show layout star ground. So both on GND net is normal schematic representation. Not an anomaly.

Now check REG1 pin 28 VDD and D1. D1 = SD103AWS Schottky. Net-(D1-A) includes C4.1, D1.2 (A), R3.2, REG1.28 (VDD). Net REG_BST includes C5.2, D1.1 (K), REG1.20 (BST). So D1 is bootstrap diode from VDD to BST. C4 = 2u2 on VDD. R3 = 10k from REG_PG to VDD (pullup for PG?). Wait R3 pin1 on REG_PG, pin2 on Net-(D1-A)=VDD. Yes pullup on power good. OK.

Hmm but wait: bootstrap diode anode should connect to VDD (the internal regulator output) and cathode to BST. Here D1.2 (A) = VDD, D1.1 (K) = BST. Correct.

Now REG_EN: R2 pin2 on REG_EN, pin1 on REG_VIN. So EN pulled up to input. OK.

Now LDO REG2 = LD39200PU33R. Pins: OUT pin1 on +3.3V, ADJ/SENSE pin2 on +3.3V, GND pin3 on GND, PG pin4 unconnected, EN pin5 on +5V, IN pin6 on +5V, EPAD pin7 on GND. Good: 3.3V LDO fed from 5V. Output +3.3V net. Note spec: 3.3V for MCUs and sensors. Good.

Now there are two 3V3-like nets: "+3.3V" and "+3V3". Let's check. Net +3.3V includes REG2 OUT, and various sensor decoupling, U1 VS, U2 VDD, U3 VCC, U4 VCC, U5, U6, U7, U8, U9, U10 VCC etc. Net +3V3 includes FCC1 VBAT? Wait NAVC1 pin1 VBAT on +3V3. Hmm. And +3V3 includes C16-C26 (FCC decoupling), C40-C48 (NAVC decoupling), R9-R14 pullups, R28-R31 pullups, connectors, SW2/3/4 pin1, U11 VCC, etc.

Wait, are +3.3V and +3V3 connected? Let's see. +3.3V net has REG2 pin1 OUT. +3V3 net — does it have REG2? No. Hmm. So we have two separate 3.3V nets? Let's check what feeds +3V3. Looking at +3V3 net members: ADC_FCC1 pin1, C16-C26, C40-C48, GPS_NAVC1 pin1, I2C3_FCC1 pin1, I2C3_NAVC1 pin1, NAVC1 pin1 (VBAT), R9-R14, R28-R31, RCIN_FCC1 pin1, SW2 pin1, SW3 pin1, SW4 pin1, SWD1 pin1, SWD2 pin1, U11 pin5, UART3_FCC1 pin1, UART4_FCC1 pin1, UART4_NAVC1 pin1, UART5_FCC1 pin1.

And +3.3V net members: C10, C12, C34, C35, C36 pin2, C54-C65, JP3 pin1, JP4 pin1, LED2 pin2, R24, R25, R37, R38, REG2 pin1, REG2 pin2, U1 pin4, U10 pin7, U10 pin8, U2 pin1, U2 pin28, U3 pin4, U4 pin8, U5 pins, U6 pins, U7 pin12, U8 pins, U9 pin4.

Hmm so +3.3V is the LDO output feeding sensors and INA219 VS and PCA9685 VDD and EEPROMs and flash and GPS VCC. +3V3 is feeding MCU VDD? Wait but FCC1 VDD pins are unconnected! Look: net 217 unconnected-(FCC1-VDD-Pad11), 218 unconnected FCC1 VDD pad27, 219 pad50, 220 pad75, 221 pad100. And FCC1 VDDA pad21 unconnected (net 222). FCC1 VBAT pad6 unconnected (net 216). FCC1 VREF+ pad20 unconnected (net 223).

Wait that's a huge problem! The FCC MCU (STM32H753VITx) has ALL its VDD pins unconnected, VDDA unconnected, VBAT unconnected, VREF+ unconnected. Let's double check. Net +3V3 includes NAVC1 pin1 VBAT but not FCC1. Hmm. Let's search FCC1 in +3V3: not present. In +3.3V: not present. So FCC1 VDD pins (11,27,50,75,100) are all on unconnected nets. That means the FCC MCU has no power! That's a severe anomaly. But wait — is this a design error or a "known limitation"? The spec doesn't mention it. Hmm but maybe the netlist is from a build where FCC power was left off? Let's look more carefully. Actually wait, maybe the netlist just didn't include them because they're connected via a net that I missed. Let's re-scan all nets for FCC1 VDD.

Search "FCC1" occurrences: net 4 ADC3_0_FCC pin18; net 11 GPIO_A_FCC pin56; net 13 pin57; net 15 pin58; net 17 pin59; net 19 pin60; net 21 pin61; net 23 pin62; net 31 HSE_IN_FCC pin5; net 33 HSE_OUT_FCC pin37; net 35 I2C1_SCL_FCC pin93; net 37 I2C1_SDA_FCC pin95; net 39 I2C2_SCL_FCC pin47; net 41 I2C2_SDA_FCC pin51; net 43 I2C3_SCL_FCC pin68; net 45 I2C3_SDA_FCC pin78; net 51 LED_A_FCC pin35; net 53 pin36; net 55 pin89; net 57 pin90; net 59 pin91; net 60 pin92; net 72 Net-(FCC1-PH0) pin12; net 124 SPI1_CS pin29; net 125 pin31; net 126 pin67; net 127 pin30; net 128 SWCLK pin77; net 130 SWDIO pin76; net 136 Net-(U11-Pad2) pin28; net 139 UART1_TX_FCC pin54; net 143 UART2_TX_FCC pin25; net 145 UART3_RX_FCC pin73 (VCAP!); net 147 UART3_TX_FCC pin48 (VCAP!); net 149 UART4_RX_FCC pin24; net 151 pin23; net 153 pin52; net 155 pin71; net 157 pin72; net 159 pin70; net 161 USB_VBUS_FCC pin69; net 166 VREF+_FCC pin13 (PH1!); net 174 unconnected BOOT0 pin94; net 175 unconnected NRST pin14; ... many unconnected.

Wait! net 145 UART3_RX_FCC includes FCC1 pin73 which is VCAP (power_out)! And net 147 UART3_TX_FCC includes FCC1 pin48 which is VCAP. That's wrong: VCAP pins (decoupling for internal core voltage) are connected to UART3 RX/TX lines! That's a serious anomaly — VCAP should go to capacitors to ground, not to UART data lines.

Also net 166 VREF+_FCC includes FCC1 pin13 which is PH1 (bidirectional), not VREF+! And VREF+ pin20 is unconnected (net 223). So VREF+ is floating and PH1 is mislabeled/connected as VREF+. Hmm.

Also FCC1 VDD pins all unconnected. FCC1 VDDA pin21 unconnected. FCC1 VBAT pin6 unconnected. FCC1 NRST pin14 unconnected (but NRST_FCC net has SW1, C31, SWD1 pin10 — wait NRST_FCC net 61 includes C31.1, SW1.1, SW1.2, SWD1.10. But FCC1 NRST pin14 is on unconnected net 175! So the reset button and SWD NRST are not connected to the MCU reset pin! That's an open connection anomaly.

Hold on. Let's look at NAVC1 too. NAVC1 VDD pins 19,32,48,64 all unconnected (nets 277-280). NAVC1 VSSA pin12 unconnected (net 281). NAVC1 NRST pin7 unconnected (net 225) while NRST_NAVC net 62 has C49, SW5, SWD2 pin10. NAVC1 VBAT pin1 is on +3V3 (good). NAVC1 VDDA pin13 on VDDA_NAVC net 164 (good). NAVC1 BOOT0 pin60 unconnected (net 224) while BOOT0_NAVC net 8 has R26 pin2 only (not MCU). Hmm.

Wait, this is suspicious. Both MCUs have all VDD pins unconnected and NRST unconnected and BOOT0 unconnected. That looks like the netlist was generated with the MCU power pins not connected — but that would mean the board doesn't work at all. Is this the "reference design" as-built? The spec says FCC populated with STM32H753VITx and NAVC with STM32F405RGTx. The spec doesn't say power pins are unconnected.

Hmm, but maybe I'm misreading. Let's look at the libpart pin names for STM32H753VITx: pin 11 VDD, 27 VDD, 50 VDD, 75 VDD, 100 VDD, 21 VDDA, 6 VBAT, 20 VREF+, 48 VCAP, 73 VCAP, 14 NRST, 94 BOOT0. In the netlist, these are all on "unconnected-(FCC1-...)" nets except pin 48 and 73 which are on UART3_TX_FCC and UART3_RX_FCC nets, and pin 13 (PH1) on VREF+_FCC net.

Wait, this strongly suggests the schematic's FCC symbol pins got mis-wired: the net labels that should be on certain pins are shifted. Let's look: net 145 UART3_RX_FCC = FCC1 pin73 (VCAP) + UART3_FCC1 pin4. net 147 UART3_TX_FCC = FCC1 pin48 (VCAP) + UART3_FCC1 pin3. So UART3 connector's TX/RX are connected to VCAP pins instead of actual UART pins. On STM32H753VI, UART3 TX = PB10 (pin46), RX = PB11 (pin47). But pin46 PB10 is unconnected (net 179) and pin47 PB11 is on I2C2_SCL_FCC (net 39). Hmm.

Actually wait. Let's look at the STM32H753VITx pinout: pin 46 = PB10, pin 47 = PB11, pin 48 = VCAP, pin 49 = VSS, pin 50 = VDD. UART3_TX is PB10 (pin46), UART3_RX is PB11 (pin47)? Actually on H7, USART3_TX = PD8 or PB10; RX = PD9 or PB11. Hmm. But here UART3_TX_FCC net has pin48 (VCAP) and UART3_RX_FCC net has pin73 (VCAP). That's clearly wrong — VCAP pins are internal regulator decoupling, must connect to capacitors to ground.

Also pin 73 = VCAP, pin 74 = VSS, pin 75 = VDD. And pin 13 = PH1. So VREF+_FCC net connects to pin13 (PH1) instead of pin20 (VREF+). And VDDA_FCC net 163 connects to C28.1 and R21.2 only — no FCC1 VDDA! FCC1 VDDA pin21 is unconnected (net 222). So VDDA analog supply of FCC is floating, while a net named VDDA_FCC exists but isn't connected to the MCU.

This pattern — power pins unconnected, VCAP tied to UART, VREF+ tied to PH1, NRST floating — looks like a systematic pin-mapping error in the FCC symbol, OR deliberate tampering. But the spec's "logged bugs" only mention barometer RESET/EOC mixed up. It does NOT mention FCC power pins unconnected. So if FCC has no VDD, the board wouldn't function — that's a major anomaly.

But wait, let's also examine NAVC1. NAVC1 VDD pins 19,32,48,64 unconnected. NAVC1 VSSA pin12 unconnected. NAVC1 NRST pin7 unconnected. NAVC1 BOOT0 pin60 unconnected. NAVC1 VBAT pin1 on +3V3 (good). NAVC1 VDDA pin13 on VDDA_NAVC (good). NAVC1 PH0 pin5 on Net-(NAVC1-PH0) with C37 (good). NAVC1 PH1 pin6 on Net-(NAVC1-PH1) with C38 (good). NAVC1 VCAP_1 pin31 unconnected (net 275), VCAP_2 pin47 unconnected (net 276). Hmm VCAP unconnected on NAVC too.

So both MCUs have VDD floating. That can't be right for a working reference design. Unless... the netlist is a "build" that has been tampered with. The task says: "decide whether the design files contain an anomaly: a deviation from the intended design that would make the board behave differently from what was intended. It could come from a design error, an assembly or sourcing mistake, or deliberate tampering."

Hmm but the spec was "written by examining the reference design" and describes intended design. If the reference design actually had VDD connected, then this netlist (a build) deviates. But maybe the reference design netlist also has these unconnected? The spec doesn't quote the netlist's MCU power connectivity. The spec says "3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC)". In the netlist, +3V3 net includes NAVC1 pin1 VBAT but NOT any VDD of either MCU. +3.3V includes neither MCU.
